title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative:
This Country Programme Outcome (CPO) seeks to address Kenya’s persistent skills gaps and mismatches, particularly in sectors such as extractives and renewable energy, where reliance on foreign expertise remains high due to insufficient local capacity. The ILO will support employers’ organizations in strengthening institutional capacity to shape demand-driven skills development and better align TVET curricula with labour market needs.
Central to the initiative is the establishment of Sectoral Skills Councils (SSCs) to foster structured dialogue between employers, training institutions, and policymakers. These councils will provide evidence-based inputs to influence curriculum reform and promote skills strategies responsive to industry demands. The CPO will also engage sectoral associations and employers’ federations to assess gaps and apply the Skills for Trade and Economic Diversification (STED) methodology to develop targeted training programmes.
The expected outcome is a more responsive and quality-driven TVET system, improved sectoral dialogue, and enhanced policymaking informed by labour market intelligence. Employers' organizations will actively shape upskilling, reskilling, and skilling programmes to ensure alignment with economic priorities. Regional collaboration with Rwanda and Zambia will foster knowledge sharing, joint advocacy, and strengthened monitoring and evaluation frameworks.
By strengthening employers' influence in skills development, the CPO will contribute to reducing youth unemployment, boosting productivity, and promoting inclusive economic growth. The initiative ultimately reinforces the role of employers’ organizations as key actors in Kenya’s education-to-employment ecosystem, ensuring skills development is rooted in market realities and national development priorities.
